analysis.title: AI rebound provides opportunity to reduce concentrated exposures
key_insights: US stocks rebounded Monday after a steep sell-off the prior week. The S&P 500 closed +4.7%, the Nasdaq 100 +6.9%, and NVIDIA +31.5% on the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO.
Last week the Nasdaq fell around 10%, its largest weekly decline since March 2020. At Friday's close it was 19.8% below its 6 October high, near bear market territory.
The S&P 500 lost 8.6% last week and is in correction territory, about 11.5% below its 6 October high.
UBS does not think the volatility signals the structural AI investment story has broken. Cloud growth, rising usage and compute demand remain supportive.

Investor focus has shifted from AI capex scale to the returns AI investment may generate. UBS expects more differentiation between platforms with visible monetization and strong balance sheets versus those reliant on debt, scarce capacity or speculative growth.

UBS keeps global and US equities at Neutral given elevated expectations, concentrated leadership and AI monetization uncertainty. A balanced portfolio holds roughly half in equities, with tech about one-third of that.
Factors to watch before changing tactical stance: pace of AI investment, compute demand, financing conditions, and the link between revenues, free cash flow and investment spending.

Recommends using strength to reduce US megacap tech concentration. Favors Eurozone equities (similar earnings growth to US, lower valuations, broader sector mix), industrials and health care, and US equal-weight strategies.

Within AI, prefers established platforms that can fund investment internally. In semis and hardware prefers compute, leading foundries and selected equipment makers. More cautious on leveraged capacity providers and names exposed to weaker capex, normalizing prices or poor utilization.

Rebalance into fixed income with intermediate duration of about 2 to 10 years. Most compelling return potential in select high yield and EM bonds yielding 7-8%, with greater credit risk and equity-like sensitivity.

Gold kept at Attractive with a forecast of USD 5,000/oz by December 2027. Support from central bank diversification, sovereign debt, geopolitics and Chinese demand, despite pressure from higher real yields, dollar strength and liquidity-driven selling.
Favors diversified commodities including copper and macro, market-neutral and fixed income relative value hedge funds as less correlated return sources.

Asian policy steadied markets before the US open. Taiwan tightened short-selling limits, Chinese exchanges eased margin-financing requirements and South Korea said it could deploy stabilization measures.

market_movers.rationale: Shares rose 31.5% on Monday after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO, driving the broader rebound.

sector_views.rationale: Preferred sector for diversifying away from tech concentration.
Reduce megacap concentration, favor quality with internal funding, compute, foundries and equipment over leveraged capacity providers.
Similar earnings growth to US, lower valuations and a broader sector mix.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Treasuries gave back a little of the prior week's risk-off rally.
Small give-back after last week's rally.
UBS keeps gold as Attractive for strategic diversification.

trade_ideas.description: Reduce overlapping US megacap tech exposure into strength and shift toward US equal-weight strategies, Eurozone equities, industrials and health care
trade_ideas.rationale: Concentrated exposure revealed portfolio weaknesses in last week's sell-off and the rebound offers a chance to rebalance.

trade_ideas.description: Rebalance into intermediate-duration fixed income (2-10 years) and select high yield and EM bonds yielding 7-8%
trade_ideas.rationale: Elevated starting yields give income and a cushion, and quality bonds hedge a growth-led downturn.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher credit risk and equity-like sensitivity in high yield and EM.

trade_ideas.description: Hold gold as Attractive with a USD 5,000/oz forecast by December 2027
trade_ideas.rationale: Central bank reserve diversification, sovereign debt, geopolitical uncertainty and Chinese demand.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher US real yields, dollar strength and liquidity-driven selling.

risk_factors: Further AI-return scrutiny and debt-dependent or capacity-scarce AI names disappointing on utilization or pricing.
Reduced holiday liquidity amplifying index swings.
Higher US real yields and dollar strength pressuring gold.
Financing conditions tightening for AI investment.
vol_and_positioning: The holiday-shortened US week ahead of Thanksgiving has reduced liquidity and may amplify index swings in either direction.
Nasdaq's roughly 10% weekly drop was its largest since March 2020, and the index sits near the 20% bear-market threshold.
UBS suggests gradual, disciplined rebalancing over all-or-nothing calls, and using rebounds to cut overlapping megacap tech positions.
geopolitical: Asian authorities intervened to steady markets: Taiwan tightened short-selling restrictions, Chinese exchanges eased margin-financing requirements, and South Korea reiterated it could deploy stabilization measures.
Government policy increasingly drives economic outcomes, which UBS cites as a reason to diversify return sources.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud growth, rising usage and continued compute demand keep the structural AI investment story intact.
tension_points.bear_case: Investor focus has shifted to AI returns, with concentrated leadership and monetization uncertainty, and firms reliant on debt, scarce capacity or speculative growth are exposed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deterioration in AI investment rates, compute demand, financing conditions or the revenue to free cash flow to investment relationship, which UBS lists as factors to watch before changing its tactical stance.

theme_stances.key_argument: Use the rebound to cut megacap tech concentration and rebalance toward quality AI platforms, diversifiers and fixed income.
theme_stances.evidence: Today's sharp rebound provides investors with an opportunity to strengthen portfolios
